L269@P5: 2.2.2. The spectrum. The analogy from Remark 2.1.6 suggests the following definition.
L270@P5: Definition 2.2.4. (i) The spectrum of a Banach ring A is the set M(A) of all
L271@P5: bounded real semivaluations | |x on A (i.e. | |x ≤ C| | for some C) provided with

L276@P5: A/Ker(| |x) is an integral valued ring. The completed fraction field of this ring
L277@P5: is called the completed residue field of x and we denote it as H(x). The bounded
L278@P5: character corresponding to x will be denoted χx : A → H(x).

L361@P7: At this point we fix a non-archimedean ground field k and start to develop
L362@P7: non-archimedean analytic geometry over k. When developing this theory we will
L363@P7: compare it from time to time to the classical theory of algebraic varieties over a
L364@P7: field. Analogously to the latter theory, we will first introduce k-Banach algebras
L365@P7: of topologically finite type and their spectra, called k-affinoid algebras and spaces.
L366@P7: Then we will construct general k-analytic spaces by pasting k-affinoid ones. Despite
L367@P7: this general similarity, many details in our theory are much subtler. We will try to
L368@P7: indicate critical moments where the theories differ.

L736@P13: Since Fact 3.2.5 is of fundamental importance, it does not make any sense to
L737@P13: deal with the case of H = 1 in the sequel. From now on, H 6= 1. The following
L738@P13: result shows that our definition of generalized localization was general enough. It
L739@P13: allows to use rational domains for all local computations on affinoid spectra.
L740@P13: Fact 3.2.7 (Gerritzen-Grauert theorem). Any kH-affinoid domain in X is a finite
L741@P13: union of H-strict rational domains in X.
L742@P13: Remark 3.2.8. This result (in the strict case) was not available in the first version
L743@P13: of rigid geometry due to Tate. For this reason, Tate simply worked with rational
L744@P13: domains and did not consider the general affinoid domains. In rigid geometry, the
L745@P13: theorem was proved by Gerritzen-Grauert, and in Berkovich geometry the nonstrict case was first deduced by Ducros. Two known rigid-theoretic proofs of this
L746@P13: result are rather long and difficult. Originally, this theorem was needed to develop
L747@P13: the very basics of analytic geometry, including Fact 3.2.5. Later it was shown in
L748@P13: [Tem3] that Fact 3.2.5 can be proved independently, and then Gerritzen-Grauert
L749@P13: theorem can be deduced rather shortly.

L752@P13: 3.3. G-topology and the structure sheaf.
L753@P13: 3.3.1. G-topology of compact domains. In order to define k-affinoid spaces we should
L754@P13: provide each spectrum X = M(A) with a certain structure sheaf OX. Naturally, we
L755@P13: would like OX to be a sheaf of k-affinoid or k-Banach algebras but then we should
